english.title: Director of insurance company fail to notify regulator of intention to propose resolution for voluntary winding up
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), a notice of a general meeting of a long-term insurer, namely **(..SPECIFY THE INSURER..), having been given, specifying the intention to propose a resolution for voluntary winding up of the insurer, you, being a director of the insurer, failed to notify the

(A)_[Prudential Regulation]_
(B)_[Financial Conduct]_

Authority as soon as practicable after you became aware of it
english.legislation: Contrary to section 366(2) and (3) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

english.notes:
(i) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the 'appropriate regulator' (either the Financial Conduct or the Prudential Regulation Authority) or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii) The PRA will be the appropriate body for the director of the insurer to inform unless the activity of effecting or carrying out long-term contracts of insurance as principal is not to any extent a PRA-regulated activity, in which case it would be the FCA.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
